sourced.citation: Act of Dec. 31, 1965, P.L. 1257, No. 511 (Local Tax Enabling Act)
sourced.note: Authorizes political subdivisions to levy earned income and other local taxes; the matrix's Act 511 cell.
Municipalities over 50,000 may tax earned income of residents and income earned in the city by nonresidents; § 902 caps the rate at 1.25 percent of income for residents and for nonresidents.
Cities of all classes may levy the taxes provided for in Ky. Const. § 181, including license fees and the occupational tax.
Counties of 300,000 or more may impose occupational license fees by order or resolution.
Cities of the first class raise revenue from taxes based on income, licenses and franchises.

findings.finding: The matrix calls the payroll tax a City of Newark tax under N.J.S.A. 40:48C-14 (restricted to specific cities). The statute's section 15, as of 10/6/2026, says any municipality may impose an employer payroll tax by ordinance at up to one percent, and routes the revenue to schools when median household income is $55,000 or more. The cell should say any municipality, not Newark only.

The matrix says the City of Wilmington levies a 1.25 percent Earned Income Tax under 22 Del. C. § 901. Chapter 9 is titled Municipal User Tax and authorizes any municipality over 50,000 people; section 902 caps both resident and nonresident rates at 1.25 percent. The cap is the statute; Wilmington's levy is its own ordinance.
